problems.title: Hot path
problems.statement: Which belong on a microsecond hot path?

options: a pre-sized array indexed by price tick
throwing an exception on a rejected order
an SPSC ring to the strategy thread

problems.solution: Rehashing and exceptions are rare but slow, exactly what ruins tails.

problems.title: Tail vs median
problems.statement: Median 2 µs, p99.9 40 µs, 10⁶ messages per day.

parts.prompt: Messages per day slower than 40 µs (≈)?

options: per-stage timestamps and histograms to find the rare events

problems.solution: About 1,000 slow messages: find what's different about them.

problems.title: Sequence gaps

options: detect the gap at 103; request a retransmit or snapshot before trusting the book

hints: Books are built from complete streams.
problems.solution: A missing update makes the book wrong in ways you can't detect later.

problems.title: Unaligned decode
problems.statement: Reading a little-endian uint32 at byte offset 3 of a packet buffer in C++.

options: memcpy into a uint32_t (and byte-swap if needed)

problems.solution: memcpy compiles to a single load where allowed, without UB.

problems.title: Rehash pause
problems.statement: An unordered_map grows from 2²⁰ to 2²¹ buckets, rehashing 10⁶ elements at ~20 ns each.
problems.solution: About 20 ms, enormous at microsecond budgets. Reserve up front.

problems.title: Throughput
problems.statement: A feed delivers 5 million messages per second at peak.
problems.solution: 200 ns per message, end to end, on one core.

problems.title: Your edge
problems.statement: Which GPU-course skills transfer directly to low-latency roles?
problems.solution: Warp specifics are GPU-only; the reasoning and discipline transfer.

problems.title: Warm path
problems.statement: The first message after 10 s of silence takes 15 µs instead of 2 µs.

options: caches/TLB/branch predictors went cold; keep the path warm with periodic dummy work

problems.solution: Some firms run "heartbeat" executions of the hot path to keep it resident.
